assessment.nobel_worthiness: The heterogeneous-firm framework reorganized international trade. It explains exporter selection, within-industry reallocation and a new channel for gains from trade. It also changed empirical work on firm-level data. Its influence extends to IO, macro and development. Its originality and reach are very high.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central contribution. Helpman has a broad record, including Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple on exports versus FDI and the earlier monopolistic-competition trade work. Redding is an important extender, with quantitative spatial and trade applications, but is less foundational. A Melitz-Helpman pairing is the cleanest.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of confirmation, a very large literature, and routine use in policy and empirical work. Timing is not a concern.
uncertainties: Krugman's 2008 prize on trade and location may be viewed as partly overlapping, although the firm-heterogeneity mechanism is distinct.
Helpman also appears in B029, so the Committee could prefer a different pairing.
Credit for firm-selection ideas also involves related contemporaneous work, for example Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum, which is not on this list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: 'Credit Cycles' (1997) shows how collateral values and borrowing limits amplify and propagate shocks. It is a basic building block of modern macro-finance and a core mechanism for financial-crisis analysis. It is important, original and widely used in both academic and central-bank models.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore are the sole authors of the foundational paper, so the credit is clear. Gertler and Gilchrist belong to the financial-accelerator tradition that follows Bernanke-Gertler. Bernanke's 2022 prize already recognized the financial-intermediation and crisis strand, so adding them would blur the lines of credit.
assessment.maturity: Nearly thirty years since publication. The mechanism is validated by the 2008 crisis and a very large derivative literature.
uncertainties: The 2022 prize on banks and financial crises may be seen as having covered part of this territory.
Empirical identification of collateral channels is more contested than the theory.
The prize is concentrated on one landmark paper plus follow-ups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The random-coefficients discrete-choice demand framework (BLP) and dynamic oligopoly methods made empirical IO quantitative. They support merger review, antitrust and welfare analysis. The methods are used throughout IO and in trade, health and environmental applications. Methodological reach is very high.
assessment.attribution: Berry-Levinsohn-Pakes (1995) is the core of the demand side. Pakes has additional foundational work on dynamic games (Ericson-Pakes), patents and estimation. The list is long, with seven names, but only the three BLP authors are needed. Bresnahan, Reiss and Benkard have real but more separable contributions, so the boundaries are somewhat fuzzy.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of continuous use, with many extensions and software implementations. Confirmation is strong.
uncertainties: Subfield proximity to my own field means I should discount any personal affinity.
Whether the Committee prefers the demand-estimation core or a broader 'new empirical IO' prize is unclear.
Some of the strongest recognition could go to Bresnahan or Pakes alone.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 1990s 'Redux' framework and the Foundations of International Macroeconomics established microfounded, welfare-based open-economy analysis. The exchange-rate disconnect work is also influential. The work underlies modern analysis of exchange-rate regimes and international policy. Importance is high, though somewhat more textbook-based than a single discovery.
assessment.attribution: Obstfeld-Rogoff (1995, 1996 and the textbook) is the shared core. Their joint credit is clear. Rogoff also appears in B039, but the contributions are separable.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of use. The disconnect puzzles remain open, so the empirical confirmation of some elements is partial.
uncertainties: Part of the contribution is synthesis and pedagogy rather than a single identifiable result.
Later work such as Gopinath's on dominant-currency pricing may reshape how credit in international price-setting is viewed.
Many relevant authors are not on this list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework with nominal rigidities is the working model of monetary-policy analysis in central banks. The contributions run from staggered pricing and policy rules to the full DSGE synthesis. The practical and conceptual impact is very high.
assessment.attribution: This is the hardest attribution problem on the list. Eight names are credited. Calvo and Taylor wrote the staggered-price building blocks, Woodford the synthesis, Gali and Gertler the empirical and theoretical development, and Christiano-Eichenbaum the estimated DSGE models. Any choice of three is contestable, and previous prizes (Phelps, Lucas, Kydland-Prescott, Sargent-Sims) overlap.
assessment.maturity: Decades of use, but the framework was stress-tested by the 2008 crisis and the 2021 inflation episode, which raises open questions.
uncertainties: Selecting three from eight is difficult, and the choice here is a judgment.
Credit overlaps with earlier prizes on rational expectations and policy rules.
Inflation developments after 2021 might lower or raise the case.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rubinstein's 1982 alternating-offers model gave a tractable, widely used theory of bargaining. The bargaining-in-markets work with Wolinsky links it to search and decentralized trade. The influence on game theory, labor, trade and political economy is substantial.
assessment.attribution: The 1982 result is Rubinstein's alone. Binmore contributed to the strategic approach, with Binmore-Rubinstein-Wolinsky (1986) linking it to Nash bargaining, and Wolinsky to market models. Rubinstein is clearly central, and a second laureate is optional.
assessment.maturity: More than forty years of confirmation. A prize is long overdue relative to the age of the work.
uncertainties: Recent game-theory and mechanism-design prizes may reduce appetite for another theory prize.
Empirical and applied testing of the model is limited, as it is mostly a theoretical benchmark.
Whether to include Wolinsky or Binmore is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bayesian persuasion and information design provide a general framework for how senders can optimally shape beliefs. The work has had a strong influence on theory and applied settings such as disclosure, platform design and regulation. Importance is high and growing.
assessment.attribution: Kamenica-Gentzkow (2011) is the founding paper. Bergemann-Morris developed the general information-design and robust-predictions program, and Morris has broader work in global games. Credit assignment between these two strands is contestable.
assessment.maturity: About fifteen years. This is mature enough for consideration, but confirmation in practice is still limited.
uncertainties: It may be too early, as applications are still maturing.
Gentzkow's broader empirical work may confound credit.
Overlap with recent prizes for mechanism design and auction theory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative data on income mobility transformed the measurement of opportunity and neighborhood effects. The work is empirically important and policy-relevant, and it set new standards for data use. The conceptual novelty is lower than in the highest-ranked theory-driven candidates.
assessment.attribution: Chetty leads the program, while Hendren and Friedman are key co-authors of the mobility, neighborhood and tax-record studies. Katz's role is mainly in the earlier Moving to Opportunity work. Joint authorship makes separating individual credit hard.
assessment.maturity: A little over a decade of major output. The most important findings are recent, and some, such as causal neighborhood effects, are still being replicated and refined.
uncertainties: It may be early for a prize, and the Committee may favor older contributions.
Chetty also appears in B027, which raises the possibility of other groupings.
The empirical findings' robustness and policy interpretation are still debated.
